purpose: Tamoxifen is mainly used to treat and help prevent certain types of breast cancer, especially cancers that are fueled by the hormone estrogen. It is used in both women and men. It can also be used to lower the risk of breast cancer in people who are at high risk of developing it.
how_it_works: Some breast cancer cells need estrogen to grow. Tamoxifen works by blocking the places on cancer cells where estrogen normally attaches, kind of like putting the wrong key in a lock so the door never opens. Without estrogen's signal, the cancer cells slow down or stop growing.
common_side_effects: Hot flashes and night sweats are very common. You might also notice mood changes, vaginal dryness or discharge, irregular periods, nausea, headaches, joint pain, or fatigue. Many of these symptoms feel similar to menopause.
warnings: Tamoxifen can rarely cause serious blood clots in the legs or lungs, so tell your doctor right away if you have leg swelling, chest pain, or trouble breathing. There is also a small risk of uterine cancer with long-term use, so report any unusual vaginal bleeding immediately. Do not take tamoxifen if you are pregnant, as it can harm an unborn baby. Avoid grapefruit and certain antidepressants like fluoxetine, as they can affect how well this medicine works.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 20 mg taken by mouth once a day, with or without food. Treatment is often continued for 5 to 10 years depending on your situation. Try to take it at the same time each day to keep it consistent.
